videos.title: COMPLETE GUIDE TOM'S SIMPLE STORAGE MOD FOR MINECRAFT

order.note: The inventory connector is the first and most important craft - it is the block that aggregates adjacent chests into one network. Chest, planks, comparator, diamond and an ender pearl.
The storage terminal second - the screen you actually interact with. Without it the connector does nothing visible.
Trims third: they are the cheap filler that lets the connector reach chests that are not physically touching it.
Cables and cable connectors only once the build outgrows one cluster.

ladder.note: Terminal ladder - each rung a real recipe step: the plain terminal, then the crafting terminal built FROM it with a crafting table and a diamond, then a wireless terminal (spyglass + ender pearl), then the advanced wireless via a smithing table.

Reach ladder: connector alone -> trims to extend the touching cluster -> cables to span distance -> cable connectors to attach a remote inventory -> filtered cable connectors to control what that inventory contributes.
Filter ladder for automation: a plain item filter, a tag filter, then the polymorphic filter.

gates.note: Both core blocks need a comparator, and the connector additionally needs a diamond and an ender pearl - so this mod cannot start before the Nether or a decent mining run, despite being marketed as the simple storage option.
The crafting terminal is built from a finished storage terminal - it is an upgrade of it, not an alternative to it.
The advanced wireless terminal is a smithing-table transform, so it is gated behind netherite-era progression.

Cables are inert unless the chain reaches the inventory connector - 'if the cable isn't connected to the inventory connector it won't work'. The connector is the root of everything, not just one component among several.

A wireless terminal must be ASSIGNED to a connector before use (right-click it at the block), and its range is finite. The guide shows a beacon in the same chunk as the terminal extending that range - an unusual, undocumented-looking gate worth surfacing.

payoff.note: One terminal reading every attached chest is the whole point - the mod's appeal is reaching that state with vanilla-ish materials and no power, cables or channels.
The crafting terminal is the second click moment: recipes pull straight from network stock.
Going wireless is the final quality-of-life step - the terminal stops being a place you walk to.

traps.note: EVERY id in this mod carries a literal 'ts.' prefix in its registry path (confirmed in the jar's lang keys, e.g. block.toms_storage.ts.inventory_connector). A quest task written as toms_storage:inventory_connector will silently fail to match. The recipe FILE names omit the prefix, which makes this easy to get wrong.

The open crate is explicitly dismissed by the guide - 'it's not really that useful honestly, many tutorials don't even mention it'. The inventory proxy is similarly niche (it re-exposes the face of the block it points at). Neither is needed for a working terminal and neither belongs on a main quest line.

The crafting terminal's cost is criticised - 'four diamonds just to add a crafting table' on top of a terminal you already built. Worth pacing as a deliberate upgrade rather than an early expectation.

The level emitter has no 'equal to' comparison, only greater/less than; the guide's workaround is to set the threshold one above the target. A quest that asks for an exact-count signal needs that caveat.

signature.note: The connector and terminal pair - this mod's identity is being the no-power, no-channel alternative to AE2 and Refined Storage.
